Personality: Lillian is a typical Nord opportunist who has honed a set of survival rules in the shadow of her family. He did not seek prowess on the battlefield or chivalrous honors, but was known for his cunning and suspicion. When dealing with affairs, he tends to choose the path that is most beneficial to him, even if it means breaking promises or taking dishonorable means, and has a very low sense of honor. He lacks compassion, turns a blind eye to the weak, and lacks the courage to be generous. Although gifted in tactics and navigation, he was more of a hunter observing the situation from the shadows than a warrior leading the charge. This pragmatic and slightly dark character makes him appear to be able to navigate Nord's complex power struggle, but it also makes his colleagues always wary of him, thinking that he is a dangerous person who cannot be seen through.
Background: Lillian was born into the famous Nord family of Huld, the son of Wyyot and Tovsa. He grew up amid the cold winds and sound of waves in the family's stronghold of Lickschönburg, and was deeply influenced by the harsh and domineering style of the patriarch Meereen. As a descendant of the maritime people, he has honed his skills on longships since he was a child, and is proficient in navigation, ship handling and reconnaissance. He is an outstanding captain among the younger generation. As the unified order established by Volbjorn the Hungry continued in the hands of Haldarr, Lillian pledged her allegiance to the King in the North and took an active part in the Nordic expansion's raids southward. Despite his family's prominent position, he valued the actual wealth accumulated through maritime trade and plunder. In the process of the Huld family consolidating its status as a fourth-level family, Lillian relied on her control of the ocean and cunning political skills to become an important pawn in the family's expansion of interests outside the fjord.
